newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES DROP ON CHICAGO PRICES.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES DROP ON CHICAGO PRICES.

text.p: Most grains futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went limit-down on Tuesday due to Chicago price movements on Monday and expectations of a good wheat crop, traders said.
Milling wheat futures dropped by the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all maturities to end at between 20,820 forints for July and 24,810 for May 1998.
"Chicago wheat prices dropped (on Monday) by the equivalent of an average 800 forints," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
He added that the wheat crop forecast released on Monday by the Agriculture Ministry also pushed prices down, and there was a strong selling pressure on the market.
Maize futures also finished lower by between 210 and 400 forints for all maturities except October which remained unchanged at 19,610 forints.
Feed barley and sunflower seed futures also went mostly limit-down while feed wheat futures remained untraded.
Total grains futures turnover rose to 1,212 lots or 534.34 million forints from Monday's 692 lots or 305.57 million forints.
Milling wheat futures accounted for half of the total turnover with 653 lots changing hands.
